bounded_hypothesis: Across the n = 237 Rub' al-Khali desert Thermoplasmatota species-representative MAGs conditioned on continuous branch-length phylogenetic covariance from the 1,914-taxon GTDB-Tk r232 ar53 FastTree (Pagel's lambda PGLS) and genome assembly quality covariates (CheckM2 completeness, contamination, log10 assembly length, and log10 contig N50), variation in the dark proteome fraction (N_dark / N_proteins_cat) is negatively associated with desert-normalized shared external RBH gene coverage (frac_rbh_desert = N_RBH / N_prot_aai) and positively associated with assembly length and contig fragmentation, while exhibiting no negative dilution with amino acid identity (AAI) to the nearest external GTDB r232 or MGnify reference genome across the observed 48.68-80.04% AAI range.
critical_issues: Corrupted GLS and OLS R-squared calculation in scripts/02_pgls_ancestry_models.py (lines 49, 76-80): y_tilde has shape (n,) while ones_tilde * mu_null has shape (n, 1), so (y_tilde - ones_tilde * mu_null) broadcasts to an (n, n) matrix and inflates rss_null by n = 237. Consequently, all reported R-squared values in DOSSIER.md (lines 93, 116-121, 131-134) and results/pgls_*.tsv are ~0.999 instead of the true values (primary PGLS R^2 = 0.46905 vs reported 0.99916; OLS R^2 = 0.49579 vs reported 0.99787; c__SW-10-69-26 R^2 = 0.50091 vs reported 0.99884; No-JAJPHT01 R^2 = 0.44408 vs reported 0.99879; frac_complete sensitivity R^2 = 0.48306 vs reported 0.99917). Repair: flatten ones_tilde to 1D before computing rss_null and regenerate all tables and dossier numbers.

Biased ML residual variance (rss / n) used for finite-sample Wald t-statistics and standard errors in scripts/02_pgls_ancestry_models.py (lines 60-68, 196-197), truncation of small p-values to 0.000000 in results/pgls_*.tsv, and substitution of normal-approximation p-values in DOSSIER.md (lines 55, 103, 107, 116-121, 131-132) that do not match the script's Student-t calculation (e.g., primary frac_rbh_desert reported as p = 7.50e-13 from normal approximation vs t_{230} p = 9.96e-12 with ML SE and p = 1.88e-11 with unbiased SE). Repair: keep sigma2_ml = rss / n strictly inside loglik, use unbiased sigma2_unb = rss / (n - p) and t_{0.975, n-p} for standard errors, t-tests, and 95% CIs, format p-values in scientific notation (%.4e) in TSV outputs, and report the 95% profile-likelihood CI for Pagel's lambda ([0.8466, 0.9568]).

Post-hoc one-sided confirmatory hypothesis framing in DOSSIER.md Section 3 Table (line 54): formulates H_0: beta_AAI <= 0 vs H_1: beta_AAI > 0 after observing a positive slope (+0.00170) while reporting a two-sided p-value, contradicting DESIGN.md (line 49, two-sided Wald t-tests) and the original reference-divergence dilution question in round5/EXTENSIONS.md. Repair: state the primary test two-sided (H_0: beta_AAI = 0 vs H_1: beta_AAI != 0), noting that negative reference-proximity dilution (beta_AAI < 0) is rejected and the positive slope is an empirical finding within the sampled range.

Unverified disjoint proteome partition claim (N_dark + N_RBH <= N_prot) in DESIGN.md (lines 17, 81), DOSSIER.md (lines 67-68, 152, 207), and scripts/03_reconciled_coupling_and_accessory.py (line 124), plus mixed denominators between observed ratios (aai_n_rbh / n_prot_aai) and permuted ratios (aai_n_rbh / n_proteins_cat) in 03_reconciled_coupling_and_accessory.py (lines 52, 68-69). N_dark (catalogue calls, UniRef50/annotation absence on 90/80 cluster reps) and N_RBH (single-genome Pyrodigal calls, DIAMOND RBH to GTDB r232/MGnify MAGs) use different callers and non-mutually-exclusive criteria, and their gene-level intersection was not checked. Repair: remove the unverified mutual-exclusivity theorem, attribute the negative ratio correlation (rho = -0.3942 vs positive independent-permutation null mean +0.3017) to differential scaling with genome size (rho = 0.9457 for N_dark vs 0.3294 for N_RBH), and use a consistent denominator in 03_reconciled_coupling_and_accessory.py.

Mischaracterization of external GTDB r232 and MGnify comparators as 'known isolate genomes' / 'known isolates' and inaccurate AAI range ('55-72%') in DESIGN.md (line 19) and DOSSIER.md (lines 106, 179). In v2_thermo_relatives_pairs.tsv and v2_thermo_relatives_report.txt, the 237 nearest comparators (229 GTDB r232 reps, 8 MGnify genomes) are predominantly uncultured environmental MAGs, and the empirical AAI range is 48.68-80.04% across all 237 representatives (52.91-80.04% across SW-10-69-26 and E2, median 64.77%). Repair: describe comparators accurately as external GTDB r232 and MGnify reference genomes (predominantly uncultured MAGs) and cite the exact empirical AAI range.
optional_improvements: Document in DESIGN.md and DOSSIER.md that midpoint rooting of the 1,914-taxon ar53 tree induces the exact same crown split on the 237 desert representatives as outgroup rooting on the 30 Halobacteriota/Thermoproteota outgroups, and that unnormalized Brownian VCV (mean-diagonal scaled) yields virtually identical PGLS slope and p-value estimates (lambda_ML = 0.9161, R^2 = 0.4753, beta_AAI = +0.00174, beta_RBH = -0.14050) to the unit-diagonal correlation matrix C.

Compute partial=00 completeness fractions directly from the assemblies of the 5 unparsed 48PRr1 MAGs (48PRr1__SemiBin_112, _141, _510, _539, _849) if full n = 237 coverage is desired in the caller-completeness sensitivity model.

Frame Section 7's unexecuted macroevolutionary ancestral reconstruction (Dollo parsimony / Count) and multi-caller benchmarking strictly as out-of-scope future extensions, since the bounded finite-cohort PGLS and descriptive accessory sharing analyses are already complete on all 237 representatives.
scope_changes_from_original: Narrows H1 from broad macroevolutionary claims of 'accessory proteome expansion' vs 'core dilution' between two classes (c__SW-10-69-26 vs c__E2) to a finite-cohort, continuous branch-length PGLS association model across the 237 desert Thermoplasmatota species representatives.

Replaces invalid few-cluster taxonomic sandwich standard errors (G = 3 orders or 7 families) with continuous phylogenetic covariance (Pagel's lambda on the 1,914-taxon ar53 FastTree) plus dominant-family (JAJPHT01) omission and within-SW-10-69-26 sensitivity analyses.

Reconciles the RBH coverage denominator from min(N_a, N_b) to the desert MAG's own protein count and replaces directional gene-gain/loss claims with descriptive dark-family occupancy tiers across the 237 genomes.
reason: The bounded finite-cohort PGLS association design is identifiable, falsifiable, and computationally executed on all 237 representatives with 100% tip mapping, and its primary negative-RBH and non-negative-AAI conditional associations remain statistically robust under independent re-verification. However, status is REVISE because (1) a 1D-to-2D NumPy broadcasting bug in 02_pgls_ancestry_models.py corrupts every reported R-squared to ~0.999 instead of ~0.44-0.50, (2) biased ML variance (RSS/n) is used in place of unbiased RSS/(n-p) for finite-sample t-tests while DOSSIER.md cites normal-approximation p-values absent from the truncated TSV outputs, (3) DOSSIER.md frames a post-hoc positive AAI slope as a one-sided confirmatory alternative hypothesis, (4) N_dark + N_RBH <= N_prot is asserted as a mutually exclusive proteome partition without verifying intersection across distinct gene callers and non-exclusive homology definitions, and (5) uncultured GTDB/MGnify MAG comparators (AAI 48.68-80.04%) are mislabelled as 'known isolate genomes' (AAI 55-72%).
